title: World Heritage Atlas Quiz Bank
description: Expanded educational question bank. General questions apply across all sites; specialized questions target exact site IDs; site_type questions target UNESCO programme keys. Each record contains an answer, explanation and reference link.

scopes.label: Specialized · this site
scopes.description: Targets one or more exact site IDs.

scopes.label: Site type
scopes.description: Targets UNESCO programme keys such as World Heritage, Global Geopark or Biosphere Reserve.

quizzes.question: Which action usually prevents the most waste before recycling is needed?
options: Buy less and reuse or repair items
Buy more single-use items made from recyclable material
Mix all waste together
Burn waste in the open
quizzes.explanation: Waste prevention and reuse avoid material use in the first place; recycling is useful but still requires collection and processing.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNEP — Beat Plastic Pollution

quizzes.question: How can a plastic wrapper dropped on a street reach the ocean?
options: It dissolves immediately in soil
Rain and drains can carry it into streams and rivers
It always stays exactly where it was dropped
It turns into harmless sand overnight
quizzes.explanation: Litter can move through drains, waterways and rivers. Keeping waste out of the environment is more effective than trying to collect it later.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNEP — Beat Plastic Pollution

quizzes.question: What is the safest general rule when observing wild animals?
options: Offer food to make photos easier
Touch young animals if they seem calm
Keep a respectful distance and never feed them
Chase them until they move into view
quizzes.explanation: Feeding or approaching wildlife can change behaviour and create danger for people and animals. Follow local rules and trained guides.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — World Heritage and sustainable tourism

quizzes.question: What is a practical way to reduce pressure on a destination's water supply?
options: Leave taps running while exploring
Assume water is unlimited wherever tourists visit
Dump oils or chemicals into drains
Avoid unnecessary water use and report leaks
quizzes.explanation: Water-saving behaviour helps destinations where residents, ecosystems and visitors share limited supplies.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Education for Sustainable Development

quizzes.question: A social post claims a heritage building is 5,000 years old but gives no source. What should you do?
options: Check an authoritative record and look for evidence
Repeat it because the post has many likes
Treat every comment as a verified source
Change the date to make the story more exciting
quizzes.explanation: Popularity is not evidence. Compare claims with authoritative records, named sources and credible research; note when information remains uncertain.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

quizzes.question: What is the best way to interpret an unfamiliar heritage place?
options: Judge it only by modern appearance
Consider its history, local context and multiple sources
Assume every monument had the same purpose
Ignore the people connected with the place
quizzes.explanation: Context helps explain why a place matters, how it changed, and how communities understand it today.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

quizzes.question: Before recording or sharing a community's ceremony, song or story, what should you do?
options: Assume public visibility means unrestricted permission
Record people secretly to keep the footage authentic
Follow community protocols and ask for permission where appropriate
Remove all community context from the caption
quizzes.explanation: Living heritage belongs to the communities that practise and transmit it. Respect consent, cultural protocols, privacy and community decisions.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Why should visitors clean mud from footwear and gear when local guidance asks them to?
options: Clean footwear makes every ecosystem identical
It guarantees that no species can ever spread
It is only about keeping shoes attractive
Mud and gear can carry seeds, organisms or pathogens between places
quizzes.explanation: Organisms can be moved unintentionally between ecosystems. Follow destination-specific biosecurity guidance, especially on islands and protected areas.
quizzes.sourceLabel: Convention on Biological Diversity — Invasive Alien Species

quizzes.question: Which visitor choice generally has the lowest impact on a sensitive site?
options: Use marked paths and follow local access rules
Climb fragile structures for a better view
Take rocks or artefacts as souvenirs
Leave food waste for animals
quizzes.explanation: Marked paths and access rules help protect fragile surfaces, habitats and visitor safety. Never remove heritage material or feed wildlife.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — World Heritage and sustainable tourism

quizzes.question: Why can protecting connected habitats be more effective than protecting isolated patches alone?
options: Every species remains in one tiny location for life
Many species need to move between feeding, breeding and shelter areas
Connections prevent all natural change
Only large animals use habitats
quizzes.explanation: Ecological connections can support movement, genetic exchange and resilience. The best approach depends on the species and landscape.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Biodiversity

quizzes.question: A coastal site faces more frequent flooding. Which is the strongest first step for planning?
options: Wait for damage before collecting any information
Protect one building while ignoring residents and ecosystems
Combine local knowledge, risk evidence and an adaptation plan
Assume historical weather will never change
quizzes.explanation: Risk-aware planning combines evidence, community experience and suitable adaptation options. Measures should fit local hazards and avoid shifting risk elsewhere.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Climate change and World Heritage

quizzes.question: If a traditional practice changes as younger people adapt it to present-day life, does that automatically make it inauthentic?
options: Yes; every detail must remain frozen forever
Yes; only museum displays count as heritage
No; communities should have no say in how it changes
No; living heritage can evolve while communities continue to recognise it
quizzes.explanation: Intangible heritage is living and transmitted between generations. Communities themselves play a central role in deciding how it is continued or adapted.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Which three symbolic realms are commonly used to explain Borobudur's vertical monument layout?
options: Kamadhatu, Rupadhatu and Arupadhatu
Earth, ocean and atmosphere
Past, present and future
Java, Sumatra and Bali
quizzes.explanation: These terms describe realms associated broadly with desire, form and formlessness in Buddhist cosmology. Interpretations should be read alongside reliable heritage resources and local expertise.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: When studying Borobudur's relief panels, what helps a visitor interpret them responsibly?
options: Assume every panel is a modern decoration
Use the sequence, iconography and authoritative interpretation instead of guessing from one panel
Touch or rub the carvings to understand their texture
Treat every panel as a record of a single literal event
quizzes.explanation: Reliefs are part of a larger architectural and narrative programme. Context, preservation guidance and expert interpretation are more reliable than a guess from an isolated image.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: The principal temple at Prambanan is dedicated to which Hindu deity?
options: Poseidon
Thor
Shiva
Quetzalcoatl
quizzes.explanation: Prambanan is a major Hindu temple compound; its central and largest temple is dedicated to Shiva.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: What is a responsible way to help conserve Prambanan's stone architecture during a visit?
options: Climb temple structures for a better photograph
Write initials on an inconspicuous stone
Remove small fragments as souvenirs
Follow barriers and do not climb, scratch or touch fragile surfaces where prohibited
quizzes.explanation: Visitor behaviour can contribute to physical wear or damage. Follow site rules and protect carved stone and structural elements.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: Why should conservation planning at Komodo consider both land and sea?
options: Terrestrial and marine habitats are connected and support linked ecological processes
The sea has no influence on island ecosystems
Only one species matters in every habitat
Marine habitats are outside nature conservation
quizzes.explanation: Komodo's importance includes terrestrial wildlife and marine biodiversity. Conservation decisions should consider ecological connections and site-specific evidence.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: What is the safest response if a Komodo dragon is nearby on a trail?
options: Try to feed it for a close-up photograph
Follow ranger instructions, keep distance and do not feed or approach it
Separate a young animal from its group
Run toward it to make it move
quizzes.explanation: Komodo dragons are wild predators. Follow park rules and trained ranger guidance; do not approach, feed or provoke wildlife.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: What is the subak system best understood as?
options: A single stone temple used only for tourism
A modern factory for rice production
A community-based cooperative system for managing irrigation water in Bali
A method for replacing all local farming traditions
quizzes.explanation: Subak connects water management, farming communities and cultural-religious institutions. It is a social and landscape system, not just a canal network.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why are water temples relevant to understanding Bali's subak landscape?
options: They exist only as decorative monuments with no local context
They prove irrigation never requires cooperation
They are unrelated to the landscape's cultural significance
They are part of the cultural and institutional relationships associated with water management
quizzes.explanation: The nominated landscape expresses relationships among water temples, agricultural practices and cooperative water management. Local practice and historical context matter.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why do researchers study the geological layer in which a fossil was found?
options: Its context helps interpret the fossil's age, environment and relationship to other evidence
The layer is irrelevant once a fossil is cleaned
All fossils from one region must be the same age
A fossil alone always provides a complete history
quizzes.explanation: Stratigraphy and geological context help researchers build and test interpretations of human evolution and past environments.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran Early Man Site

quizzes.question: Which approach is most appropriate when a new fossil discovery is reported?
options: Move it immediately and discard location notes
Document its location and context, then assess it using scientific methods
Identify its species from a social-media photo alone
Assume it changes all existing scientific knowledge at once
quizzes.explanation: Documentation and context preserve scientific value. Conclusions should follow careful analysis and comparison with existing evidence.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran Early Man Site

quizzes.question: Why can a large protected area spanning different elevations support varied ecosystems?
options: Elevation has no effect on habitat
Every species requires exactly the same climate
Temperature, moisture and habitat conditions can change with elevation
Only the highest point can support life
quizzes.explanation: Elevation gradients can create different habitat conditions and ecological communities. The actual pattern varies across the landscape.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Lorentz National Park

quizzes.question: What is a sound reason to combine local knowledge with biodiversity research in a landscape like Lorentz?
options: Local knowledge should automatically replace every scientific method
Scientific data means local communities should not be consulted
Only observations from tourists are useful
Different evidence sources can complement each other when collected and interpreted respectfully
quizzes.explanation: Research and local knowledge can answer different questions. Collaboration should respect rights, protocols, evidence quality and community consent.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Lorentz National Park

quizzes.question: What is central to a place being inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
options: Its Outstanding Universal Value, assessed against the Convention's criteria
Its popularity on social media
The number of souvenirs sold nearby
Its age alone, regardless of significance
quizzes.explanation: World Heritage inscription depends on Outstanding Universal Value and the applicable criteria, alongside requirements for protection and management.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — About World Heritage

quizzes.question: What does the distinction between cultural, natural and mixed World Heritage properties describe?
options: The number of people allowed to visit every day
The kinds of heritage values for which the property is recognised
Whether a site must charge an entry fee
Whether a property has a visitor centre
quizzes.explanation: The categories reflect the basis of recognition under the World Heritage Convention; they are not visitor-service or popularity ratings.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — About World Heritage

quizzes.question: Does a Tentative List entry mean a property is already inscribed on the World Heritage List?
options: Yes; every Tentative List property is already inscribed
Yes, but only for natural properties
No; it is a property a State Party may consider for a future nomination
It means the property has been removed from heritage consideration
quizzes.explanation: A Tentative List is an inventory of properties a State Party may consider for nomination. A Tentative List entry is not the same as inscription.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tentative Lists

quizzes.question: Who submits and updates a country's World Heritage Tentative List?
options: Any visitor by adding a pin to an online map
A travel company acting without the country's involvement
A local business with no official process
The State Party, through its national processes
quizzes.explanation: Tentative Lists are submitted by States Parties. A site's presence should not be presented as an inscription or guaranteed future nomination.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tentative Lists

quizzes.question: What makes a UNESCO Global Geopark more than a collection of interesting rocks?
options: It connects internationally significant geological heritage with protection, education and sustainable development
It is only a list of mineral shops
It must exclude all communities from the area
It recognises only built monuments
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO Global Geoparks take a place-based approach that connects geological heritage with wider natural and cultural values, education and sustainable local development.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: How should a geopark's geological sites generally be managed?
options: Encourage visitors to remove representative rocks
Conserve their geological heritage while supporting education and responsible local development
Treat geology as unrelated to local culture and livelihoods
Promote unlimited access regardless of site sensitivity
quizzes.explanation: Geoconservation, education and sustainable development are complementary goals. Local rules and site-specific conservation needs still apply.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the core, buffer and transition areas in a biosphere reserve model?
options: They rank areas from most famous to least famous
They mean every activity is allowed in every zone
They help combine conservation with compatible research, activities and sustainable development
They separate people from nature in all circumstances
quizzes.explanation: Biosphere reserves use zonation to support conservation in core areas while allowing compatible activities, cooperation and sustainable development in surrounding zones.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Which approach best reflects the Man and the Biosphere Programme?
options: Protect nature while ignoring how local people live
Focus only on visitor numbers
Replace every local management institution with tourism operators
Connect biodiversity conservation with research, learning and sustainable livelihoods
quizzes.explanation: The programme promotes approaches that connect people and nature, conservation and sustainable development, with learning and cooperation across landscapes.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Which is an example of intangible cultural heritage?
options: A community's living performance, craft knowledge, oral tradition or festive practice
Only a stone building with no associated practice
Only an item stored in a museum
A tradition that the community no longer recognises but outsiders impose
quizzes.explanation: Intangible cultural heritage includes practices, expressions, knowledge and skills that communities recognise and transmit between generations.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Who should play a central role in safeguarding a living heritage practice?
options: Only outside researchers
The communities and practitioners who recognise and transmit it
Only a tourism company
Visitors who have no connection with the practice
quizzes.explanation: Safeguarding should respect the people who practise and transmit the heritage, including their rights, consent and choices about how it continues.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: What is the broad aim of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network?
options: Rank cities only by the number of historic monuments
Replace local culture with a single global style
Use creativity and cultural industries as part of sustainable urban development
Certify that every business in a city is creative
quizzes.explanation: The network encourages cooperation among cities that place culture and creativity within sustainable development strategies.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network

quizzes.question: Which action fits the idea of a creative city best?
options: Measure success only by souvenir sales
Exclude community artists from city planning
Treat creativity as unrelated to jobs or public life
Support local creators and connect culture with inclusive urban development
quizzes.explanation: Creative-city approaches connect cultural activity with social, economic and urban development, while respecting local diversity and community participation.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network

quizzes.question: A heritage site is closed because local authorities issue a severe-weather warning. What should a visitor do?
options: Follow official instructions and choose a safe alternative
Enter through a side gate before it gets busy
Ignore the warning if the sky looks clear
Ask other visitors to vote on whether the closure matters
quizzes.explanation: Preparedness and coordinated response help protect visitors, communities and heritage. Follow current official guidance rather than judging the hazard from appearances.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Reducing Disaster Risks at World Heritage Properties

quizzes.question: Where should an old phone or spent battery go when a destination offers a dedicated e-waste collection point?
options: Into a river so the materials can separate
To the designated collection or approved take-back service
Into any mixed litter bin
Buried beside a walking trail
quizzes.explanation: Electronics and batteries may contain materials that require specialised handling. Use a collection or take-back route provided by the local system.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNEP — Global E-waste Monitor

quizzes.question: Which action helps prevent food waste during a trip?
options: Order more than needed because leftovers always disappear
Leave perishable food in the sun for the next visitor
Plan portions, store food safely and take suitable leftovers when permitted
Throw edible food away before checking local options
quizzes.explanation: Prevention is usually preferable to managing waste later. Food safety and local rules still apply when storing or sharing leftovers.
quizzes.sourceLabel: FAO — Food Loss and Food Waste

quizzes.question: Why should visitors stay on marked paths in fragile dunes or vegetation?
options: So that every visitor sees exactly the same scenery
Because trails are only for people who walk quickly
To avoid learning about nearby habitats
To reduce trampling, erosion and damage to sensitive plants
quizzes.explanation: Marked routes can help limit pressure on fragile ground and guide people away from sensitive or hazardous areas.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sustainable Tourism

quizzes.question: You record a wildlife observation for a citizen-science platform. Which information makes the record more useful?
options: An exact location when safe to share, date, evidence and an honest confidence level
A dramatic species name even when uncertain
A copied location from an unrelated post
An edited image with no explanation
quizzes.explanation: Observation records are more useful when their evidence and context can be assessed. Avoid sharing precise locations of vulnerable species when doing so could put them at risk.
quizzes.sourceLabel: GBIF — What is GBIF?

quizzes.question: Which approach best reduces the energy impact of a visitor facility over time?
options: Run equipment at full power even when unused
Improve energy efficiency and use cleaner energy where feasible
Replace maintenance with decorative lighting
Keep doors open while air-conditioning runs
quizzes.explanation: Efficiency reduces unnecessary demand; cleaner energy can further reduce emissions depending on the energy system and project.
quizzes.sourceLabel: International Energy Agency — Energy Efficiency

quizzes.question: A sign asks visitors to remain outside a sacred room during a ceremony. What is the respectful response?
options: Enter quietly because ceremonies are public
Film through the doorway without asking
Respect the restriction and ask site staff about appropriate ways to learn
Move the sign to take a photograph
quizzes.explanation: Cultural protocols can govern access, recording and participation. Follow local guidance and do not assume every space or practice is open to visitors.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Ethics and Intangible Cultural Heritage

quizzes.question: Which is the strongest sign that tourism may be contributing to local wellbeing?
options: Visitor numbers rise but local people have no voice
All local products are replaced by imported souvenirs
Visitors are encouraged to bypass local services
Local people participate in decisions and can benefit through fair opportunities
quizzes.explanation: Sustainable tourism should account for community participation, local values and the distribution of benefits—not just the number of arrivals.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sustainable Tourism

quizzes.question: What is a useful first step when improving access for visitors with different disabilities?
options: Consult people with disabilities and identify practical barriers across information, routes and services
Assume one ramp solves every access need
Publish access information only after visitors arrive
Remove seating so paths look wider
quizzes.explanation: Accessibility works best when people with different needs are consulted and information is clear before a visit. Solutions should respond to the actual site context.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UN Tourism — Accessible Tourism

quizzes.question: When snorkelling near a coral reef, what should you do?
options: Stand on coral for a better view
Keep fins and hands away from coral and avoid disturbing marine life
Touch or collect small coral fragments
Feed fish to gather them for a photograph
quizzes.explanation: Coral and associated marine life can be damaged by contact and disturbance. Follow local marine-protection rules and guide instructions.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Ocean

quizzes.question: A photograph of a historical object circulates online with no date or location. What is the most responsible caption?
options: State its exact origin based on a guess
Copy a confident comment as the source
Describe what is visible and mark the date, origin and attribution as unverified until checked
Remove uncertainty so the post looks authoritative
quizzes.explanation: Clear provenance distinguishes observation from interpretation. Do not turn an uncertain attribution into a verified fact.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Media and Information Literacy

quizzes.question: Why should a site manager regularly review a risk register instead of preparing one only once?
options: Risks never change after a plan is written
A risk register is mainly a marketing document
Old risks should be hidden from new staff
Hazards, exposure, site conditions and mitigation measures can change over time
quizzes.explanation: Risk monitoring supports preparedness and helps teams adapt plans as conditions, knowledge and responsibilities change.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Reducing Disaster Risks at World Heritage Properties

quizzes.question: Which sequence best describes Borobudur's broad physical structure?
options: A pyramidal base with square terraces, circular platforms and a monumental stupa
A single flat courtyard with no upper platform
Five circular courtyards and a separate palace
A tower surrounded by defensive walls
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO describes Borobudur as a monument arranged in three broad tiers, crowned by a monumental stupa.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: How many openwork stupas stand around Borobudur's three circular platforms, according to the UNESCO World Heritage description?
quizzes.explanation: The World Heritage Centre describes 72 openwork stupas around the circular platforms, each containing a Buddha statue.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: Which epic is illustrated by reliefs on Prambanan's temples?
options: The Epic of Gilgamesh
The Odyssey
The Ramayana
The Mahabharata only
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO's description notes reliefs illustrating the Ramayana on the temples within the compound.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: Which three great Hindu divinities are associated with Prambanan's principal temples?
options: Zeus, Hera and Athena
Odin, Thor and Freyja
Isis, Osiris and Horus
Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma
quizzes.explanation: The Prambanan compound includes temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma, as described by UNESCO.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: Which biogeographical region is associated with Komodo National Park in the UNESCO description?
options: Wallacea, between the Australian and Sunda ecosystems
The Arctic tundra
The Amazon basin
The Himalayan plateau
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO highlights the park's location in the Wallacea biogeographical region, between the Australian and Sunda ecosystems.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: Which combination best reflects the ecological variety described for Komodo National Park?
options: Only a single urban habitat
Dry savannah and other terrestrial habitats alongside coral-rich marine waters
Only permanent snow and glaciers
An ecosystem without terrestrial animals
quizzes.explanation: The UNESCO description links rugged dry island habitats with rich coastal and marine ecosystems; both are part of the property's conservation value.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: The UNESCO title connects Bali's subak system with which philosophy?
options: Ubuntu
Wabi-sabi
Tri Hita Karana
Stoicism
quizzes.explanation: The property's official name describes the subak system as a manifestation of the Tri Hita Karana philosophy.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why is the Bali designation best understood as a cultural landscape rather than one isolated temple?
options: It refers only to a single hotel
It has no relationship to farming or water management
It represents only a natural volcano with no human history
It brings together water temples, lakes, watersheds and subak landscapes as a connected property
quizzes.explanation: The listed property includes several components that express relationships among water, farming, temples and the wider landscape.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why should a fossil find from Sangiran be documented together with its geological and archaeological context?
options: Context can help interpret age, environment and how the evidence relates to other finds
Context is unimportant once a specimen is photographed
Every fossil from the same site must have the same age
A social-media label is enough to establish a fossil's age
quizzes.explanation: Sangiran's significance relates to fossil and geological evidence. Context helps researchers build and test interpretations rather than relying on an isolated object.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran

quizzes.question: Which statement is most responsible when sharing a claim about a new fossil discovery?
options: It definitely rewrites all human history
A strong claim needs documented provenance and scientific assessment
Its age can be known from colour alone
The most dramatic online explanation is always the most reliable
quizzes.explanation: Evidence, context and review are necessary before turning a fossil discovery into a broad claim about human evolution.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran

quizzes.question: What helps explain the range of habitats associated with Lorentz National Park?
options: All parts of the park share identical environmental conditions
Only the park boundary creates biodiversity
Its broad landscape spans very different elevations and environmental conditions
The park contains no significant elevation change
quizzes.explanation: Lorentz covers a vast and varied landscape, so elevation and environmental gradients help explain its different habitats.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Lorentz National Park

quizzes.question: Which approach is most appropriate when research or conservation activities could affect Indigenous communities connected to a landscape?
options: Collect knowledge without explaining how it will be used
Assume outsiders should make every decision
Publish sensitive cultural information automatically
Engage communities respectfully, recognise rights and follow applicable consent and local protocols
quizzes.explanation: Conservation and research should respect communities' rights, knowledge, participation and protocols, especially where activities may affect cultural practices or access.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Ethics and Intangible Cultural Heritage

quizzes.question: Does World Heritage inscription mean that no further site management is needed?
options: No; protection, conservation and management remain ongoing responsibilities
Yes, inscription protects a property automatically forever
Yes, unless visitor numbers increase
No; the site must be converted into a museum
quizzes.explanation: Inscription recognises a property's significance, but States Parties and site managers still need effective protection, monitoring and management.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — About World Heritage

quizzes.question: Why might the wider setting of a World Heritage property matter?
options: It matters only if it contains a gift shop
Changes outside a mapped boundary can still affect views, relationships or attributes that contribute to the property's value
It can never affect the property's values
A buffer zone is always identical to the property itself
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO notes that development in the wider setting can threaten the relationship between a property and its surroundings; exact effects depend on the site.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: Can the World Heritage Committee examine a nomination for a property that has never been included on the State Party's Tentative List?
options: Yes, every local proposal goes directly to the Committee
Yes, if a travel operator supports it
No; inclusion on the Tentative List is a prerequisite for consideration
Only if a social-media campaign is sufficiently large
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO states that a property must already be included on the State Party's Tentative List before its nomination can be considered.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tentative Lists

quizzes.question: What is a sound way for a State Party to prepare or revise its Tentative List?
options: Treat it as a permanent list that cannot change
Let visitors add sites directly without review
Include only sites already inscribed on the World Heritage List
Involve relevant stakeholders and rights-holders and update the list through national processes
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO encourages participation by site managers, local and regional governments, communities, Indigenous peoples and other stakeholders in Tentative List processes.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Nominations

quizzes.question: What does a bottom-up approach mean in the context of a UNESCO Global Geopark?
options: Local communities take part in shaping initiatives alongside protection, education and sustainable development
All decisions are made by visiting tourists
Only international scientists may contribute
Geological heritage is separated from local life
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO describes Global Geoparks as using a bottom-up approach that involves local communities alongside protection, education and sustainable development.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — UNESCO Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: Which visitor behaviour best supports geoconservation in a geopark?
options: Chip pieces from an outcrop to take home
Leave geological features in place and follow site guidance
Write names on fossil-bearing rocks
Create new shortcuts through sensitive formations
quizzes.explanation: Geological features are part of the heritage being protected and interpreted. Visitors should follow site rules and avoid damaging or removing material.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — UNESCO Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: In a typical biosphere-reserve zonation model, which area is generally associated with sustainable human activities and development across the wider landscape?
options: The core area only, where all development is the primary purpose
An area outside every biosphere reserve
The transition area
A zone reserved only for souvenir sales
quizzes.explanation: The transition area is where communities, authorities and partners can work toward sustainable resource use and development compatible with the reserve's goals; arrangements vary by place.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Why are biosphere reserves often described as places for learning about sustainable development?
options: They exist only to restrict research
They remove communities from all decisions
They guarantee that no environmental problem can occur
They connect conservation, research, education and collaboration with communities and partners
quizzes.explanation: The Man and the Biosphere Programme promotes places where people can test and demonstrate approaches that connect biodiversity conservation with sustainable development.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Which is an example of intangible cultural heritage under the 2003 Convention?
options: Knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe, transmitted by communities
Only a newly built visitor centre
Only a printed map
Only an object separated from its community
quizzes.explanation: The Convention covers living practices, expressions, knowledge and skills recognised by communities, including knowledge concerning nature and the universe.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: What is a responsible approach to documenting a living heritage practice for an inventory?
options: Publish every detail even when the community objects
Work with the community, describe it in context and respect consent and local protocols
Treat the inventory as an outsider's ranking of cultures
Assume a recorded video alone guarantees the practice will continue
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO emphasises the participation of communities in identifying and defining intangible heritage; documentation supports safeguarding but does not replace living transmission.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Involvement of Communities

quizzes.question: Which option is one of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network's recognised creative fields?
options: Glacier engineering
World Heritage inscription status
Gastronomy
Airport management
quizzes.explanation: The Network's seven creative fields include Crafts and Folk Art, Design, Film, Gastronomy, Literature, Media Arts and Music.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network

quizzes.question: What is a key purpose of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network?
options: To certify every building in a city as World Heritage
To replace local cultural organisations with one global institution
To rank cities only by annual tourist arrivals
To help cities cooperate and use culture and creativity in sustainable urban development
quizzes.explanation: The Network promotes cooperation among cities that place culture and creativity within sustainable development strategies; it is a distinct designation from World Heritage inscription.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network
